name: Match Resolver
description: Finds the matches, clears them, and lets what falls make more. Detection is run-length in both axes over the grid, and the resolver's real work is the CASCADE: clearing drops the pieces above, dropping creates new lines, and the loop continues until a pass finds nothing. Each pass is announced separately so scoring can escalate per step, which is where the genre's entire dopamine curve lives. Special pieces are created by match SHAPE rather than by length alone — a five in a row and an L of five are different rewards — and the shape rules are declared here because they are the difference between two match-3 games that otherwise look identical. The resolver owns the board outright -- its size, its contents and its refills -- and owns no score, no timer and no objective.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Board width in cells. Declared here because the board is this component's own: an earlier draft depended on world.tile_grid for it, which is a TERRAIN grid publishing elevationAt and surfaceAt and has nothing a match-3 board can use.

inputs.name: minimumMatch
inputs.description: Pieces in a line before it clears.

inputs.name: pieceTypes
inputs.description: Distinct ordinary piece types. Fewer means more accidental cascades; more means a sparser board.

inputs.name: specialRules
inputs.description: Match shapes that create special pieces, keyed by shape. The line between one match-3 and another.

inputs.name: gravityDirection
inputs.description: Which way cleared space is refilled from.

outputs.name: cascadeDepth
outputs.description: Passes resolved since the last player move.

outputs.name: lastCleared
outputs.description: Pieces removed by the most recent pass.
